text.p: Finnnish telecommunications major Nokia Oy said on Tuesday it expected cash-flow for the full year to be neutral or slightly positive.

In the first quarter, cash-flow was 1.8 billion markka positive despite strong growth, but this could not be sustained every quarter, Martin Sandelin, Nokia's head of investor relations, told an analyst briefing.
"With all likelihood, we will be cash-flow neutral to slightly positive," Sandelin said. @

Asked to specify what Nokia's net sales growth in the first quarter would have been excluding currency effects, he said growth excluding that and disposed operations would have been 46 percent, compared to 43 percent reported.

Nokia's first-quarter net sales rose to 11.3 billion markka from 7.9 billion in the year-ago period, and pre-tax profit surged to 1.45 billion markka from 399 million. First-quarter operating profit was 1.46 billion markka versus 512 million. @

Sandelin said some currency hedging losses were booked at the operating level and the net financial items -- a 10 million markka charge versus a 113 million charge in Q1 1996 -- included some dividends and share sales.
Asked to comment on the level of net financial items in the coming quarters, he said the "likely range" was somewhere between the first quarters this year and last year.
